name: Polyunsaturated fat
what_is:
Polyunsaturated fats have more than one double bond in their chain. They fall into two main families: omega-3 and omega-6.

Omega-3 is abundant in oily fish, walnuts, flaxseed and chia. Omega-6 in sunflower, corn and soybean oil.

On a nutrition label they are a voluntary field in almost every market, and where they appear they do so as a single number: omega-3 and omega-6 together, undifferentiated.

Some products declare omega-3 separately, but that is an additional nutrition claim, not part of the mandatory panel.
why_botia:
BOTIA flags polyunsaturated fat because the figure groups two families the body does not use in the same way, and the label does not separate them.

A product can declare a high figure while providing almost only omega-6. Whether the ingredient list shows sunflower oil or walnuts changes a great deal about what that number means.
can_1: Read the declared value, where it exists, and keep its unit and its basis.
can_2: State that the figure groups omega-3 and omega-6 without distinguishing them.
can_3: Link to the omega-3 record and to the ingredients in the list that provide each family, where they can be identified.
cannot_1: Say how much is omega-3 and how much omega-6. The figure groups them and the label does not break them down unless declared voluntarily.
cannot_2: Work them out by subtracting other fats from the total.
cannot_3: Treat an undeclared value as zero.
cannot_4: Equate polyunsaturated fat with omega-3. Omega-3 is a subset, not the same thing.
